twoHalves.heading: The two halves of being a developer
twoHalves.intro: Jiki teaches you how to code (in the most fun and effective way!) and how to build real things using the same technologies the pros use. From day one.
twoHalves.codeBody: Every core concept, with detailed video explanations, and hundreds of exercises and projects to practice on

learnToCode.heading: Learn to <word>Code</word>
learnToCode.intro: Master coding, the core skill we use to communicate our desires to a computer. We'll help you <highlight>build rock solid coding foundations</highlight>.

demo.stageDescription: An animation of the Jiki app: a learner runs a space-invaders exercise, the code moves the laser cannon off the edge of the grid, they ask Jiki for help, correct the boundary from 20 to 11, and the exercise passes.
demo.instr1: The aliens are scattered across three rows, and some columns have more than one.
demo.instr2: You have three functions to work with:
demo.fnRight: moves your laser cannon one column to the right
demo.fnLeft: moves it one column to the left
demo.instr3: There are 11 columns. Move off either edge and you lose, so keep track of where you are.
demo.scenarioTitle: Three rows: aliens spread across all three rows
demo.verdictPending: Run your code to see whether this scenario passes.
demo.verdictFail: Your code hit an error while it was running. Fix the error message above.
demo.verdictPass: All six aliens destroyed. Nice work!
demo.errorTitle: Oh no, you've gone too far!
demo.errorBody: Your laser cannon moved off the right edge of the screen. Remember to track your position and reverse direction at the end.
demo.chat2: My cannon keeps going off the edge of the screen.
demo.chat3: Let's look at the line you just wrote. You turn around once position reaches 20 — but how many columns does the grid actually have?
demo.chat5: That's it. position never reaches 20, so move_left() never runs. Change that boundary to 11 and the cannon will turn at the last column.
demo.successBody: All tests passed! You've successfully completed this exercise.

meetJeremy.intro: Hi there! 👋 I'm Jeremy, and I've helped over millions of people level up their coding skills, all around the world.
meetJeremy.developerDetail: Full stack • 35 years experience • Codes in 20+ languages (including my own!) • AI Degree (from 2005) • Patented Heart Surgery AI system
meetJeremy.teacherDetail: 20 years experience • 3M+ people taught • Founded four education companies
meetJeremy.entrepreneurDetail: Founder of multiple for-good orgs including Exercism, Kaido, Thalamus, and more • Runs one of the world's largest OSS projects
meetJeremy.story: Coding has been at the center of my life since I was 8. It's taught me creativity, problem solving, and critical thinking. And it's allowed me to have a career that I've loved, building companies across education, medicine and artificial intelligence.
meetJeremy.why: I've built Jiki because I want to share that with you. I want you to be able to access the same joy and benefits that coding has given to me. And I believe that learning to code should be fun. The software development industry is changing fast. Agentic coding is becoming the norm. I'm dedicated to taking you on that journey and making sure that whether you want a career in tech or just want to know what's going on, you can. I hope you'll come and join me!
meetJeremy.quote: You learn to write code by writing code to solve problems that match, and push, your abilities. Jeremy is a master teacher.

faqs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.q1a1: The Learn to Code exercises — the core learn-to-code curriculum — are completely free. No card, no trial, no catch.
faqs.q2: How much time will I need to spend each week on the course?
faqs.q2a: You can spend as long or as little as you like. Most people get through Learn to Code in 12–20 weeks at around 5–10 hours a week. Learn to Build is ongoing — you can dip in and out as new episodes go up, and join livestreams when it suits you.
faqs.q3: How hard is the course? How smart do I need to be?
faqs.q3a1: The course is designed to be accessible to everyone, regardless of your background. We don't believe you need to be "smart" to learn to code. But you do need to put in the effort and be willing to be challenged.
faqs.q3a2: But if you put in the effort, ask for help when you get stuck, and embrace the challenge, you'll be amazed at how far you can go in a short time.
faqs.q4a1: Yes — you can sign up and start the free Learn to Code curriculum today.
faqs.q4a2: The first Learn to Build session will be in mid-June. You can sign up for a reminder once you're inside.
faqs.q5: I already signed up to the Bootcamp - is this different?
faqs.q5a1: Thanks for being part of the Bootcamp! Jiki is the next stage in the evolution of our Bootcamp. Most of the exercises you solved will appear in Jiki along with lots more. We've also broken down the 3 hour videos into smaller, 5-10 minute chunks to make watching easier!
faqs.q5a2: As a member of the Bootcamp, you'll automatically get Jiki Premium for Life. This applies to both the initial Learn to Code course and future courses.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Can I try Jiki for free?
faq.a1: Yes! You can sign up for free and use the Basic plan for as long as you like. Upgrade to Premium whenever you need full access — there's no obligation.
faq.q2: Is there a minimum contract length?
faq.a2: No minimum contract — Premium is billed monthly and you can cancel at any time from your account settings.
faq.q3: What happens if I cancel my Premium subscription?
faq.a3: You'll keep Premium access until the end of your current billing period, and then your account will move back to the Basic plan. You don't lose any of your progress — you just lose access to Premium-only features.
faq.q4: Do you offer discounts for students or those who can't afford Premium?
faq.q5: Can I upgrade or downgrade later?
faq.a5: Absolutely. You can upgrade to Premium at any time from your account, and you can cancel just as easily whenever you'd like.
faq.a4: We want Jiki to be accessible to everyone. If cost is a barrier, please <link>get in touch</link> and we'll do what we can to help.

changelog.subtitle: Recent improvements we've shipped to Jiki.

learnToBuildLaunch.title: Launched Learn to Build
learnToBuildLaunch.description: Jeremy's new series, where he builds real, useful projects from scratch alongside learners, is now live.

milestones6To10.title: Launched Milestones 6-10 on Learn to Code
milestones6To10.description: Five new milestones are now live on the Learn to Code track, extending the journey well beyond the fundamentals.

jikiLaunch.title: Launched Jiki!
jikiLaunch.description: Jiki is officially live (albeit in beta!)

now.label: Now
now.summary: What we're focused on this month.

learnToBuild.title: Launched Learn to Build
learnToBuild.description: Jeremy's brand new series is now live, where he builds real, useful projects from scratch alongside learners. Each project is broken into bite-sized lessons that show not just the code, but the thinking, mistakes, and decisions that go into shipping software.

launchBugs.title: Ironing out launch bugs
launchBugs.description: Now that Jiki is live, we're squashing bugs and smoothing rough edges as real learners use the platform. Expect a steady stream of small fixes and quality-of-life improvements across the app.

earlyFeedback.title: Responding to early feedback
earlyFeedback.description: We're reading every message, support thread, and suggestion that comes in. The most impactful pieces of feedback are being turned into tweaks and small features so the experience improves week by week.

foundations.title: Stabilising the foundations
foundations.description: Behind the scenes we're tightening up reliability, performance, and observability so we have a rock-solid base to build the next wave of features on. Less visible, but the most important work we can do right now.

betaToLive.title: Move from Beta to Fully Live
betaToLive.description: Jiki is currently in beta. Once the launch dust settles, we'll drop the beta label and graduate to a fully-live product, with stronger guarantees around reliability, a clearer pricing story, and a polished onboarding flow. This is also when we'll send the launch email to the Exercism community and kick off promotional pushes with our partners.

deepDiveVideos.title: Add Deep Dive Videos
deepDiveVideos.description: Long-form videos that go beyond the core lessons to explore concepts in real depth. Perfect for learners who want to understand the why behind the how, and to see how ideas connect to the wider world of programming.

newLanguages.title: Launch multiple new languages
newLanguages.description: Starting in August, we're bringing Jiki to learners in their own language, translating the whole interface and curriculum, not just the marketing pages. It kicks off with our <link>community translatathon</link> over the weekend of July 31st to August 2nd.

pythonVersion.title: Launch Python version
pythonVersion.description: Arriving in September, a fully-fledged Python track that mirrors the depth of our JavaScript curriculum. Same exercise philosophy, same step-through visualiser, same level of polish, but with Python as the language of instruction.

future.label: Future
future.summary: On the horizon. Subject to change as we learn.

moreLanguages.title: Add more languages
moreLanguages.description: Building on August's first wave, we'll keep translating Jiki into more spoken languages through the rest of the year, so even more learners can use the platform in their native tongue. We'll prioritise based on demand from the community and where we can have the biggest impact.

sql.title: Launch SQL
sql.description: Later in the year, we'll add SQL to Jiki, giving learners a hands-on way to understand databases and querying with the same step-through, learn-by-doing approach as the rest of the curriculum.
